question: In which of the following states is there hardly any differences in day and night temperatures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala lies on the coast (Malabar Coast) close to the Equator and is surrounded by the Arabian Sea on the west and the Western Ghats on the east. Because of this strong maritime (moderating) influence, its diurnal range of temperature — the difference between day and night temperatures — is very small. (केरल — दिन-रात के तापमान में बहुत कम अंतर)

• Water heats up and cools down much more slowly than land, so coastal areas have equable (moderate) climates — cooler days and warmer nights.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rajasthan has a hot desert (arid) climate. Sand heats and cools rapidly, so the Thar Desert shows an extreme diurnal range — scorching days and very cold nights.

• Punjab and Bihar lie in the interior of the northern plains and experience a continental climate with hot summers, cold winters and a large day–night temperature difference.

NOTE

• Continentality — the farther a place is from the sea, the greater the extremes of temperature.

• Kerala's climate type is tropical monsoon; it receives rain from both the South-West monsoon and the retreating (North-East) monsoon, and gets the first onset of the monsoon in India (around 1 June).

question: For which dance form did Vasundhara Doraswamy get Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vasundhara Doraswamy, the eminent dancer and guru from Mysuru, Karnataka, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2019 in the field of Bharatanatyam. (वसुंधरा दोराईस्वामी — भरतनाट्यम)

• She is also a recipient of the Padma Shri and has worked extensively on dance for social causes and for children with special needs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama, set up in 1952 with its headquarters at New Delhi.

• Its highest honour is the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna), while the Akademi Puraskar (Award) is given annually to outstanding artistes.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; it was earlier known as Sadir/Dasi Attam.

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Padma Subrahmanyam, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Alarmel Valli, Mallika Sarabhai.

question: The dancers Padma Subrahmanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are great exponents of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Padma Subrahmanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are all celebrated exponents of the classical dance form Bharatanatyam. (भरतनाट्यम)

◦ Padma Subrahmanyam — noted for reviving the Karanas described in the Natya Shastra.

◦ Alarmel Valli — famous for the Pandanallur style of Bharatanatyam.

◦ Yamini Krishnamurthy — trained in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan.

◦ Anita Ratnam — known for blending Bharatanatyam with contemporary idioms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and has three main elements — Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance) and Natya (dramatic element).

• Its repertoire order is Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam → Tillana.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised in India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following states won the Santosh Trophy in Riyadh in March 2023 after a gap of 54 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Karnataka won the 76th Santosh Trophy in March 2023, defeating Meghalaya in the final played at the King Fahd International Stadium, Riyadh (Saudi Arabia). It was Karnataka's title after a gap of 54 years (their previous win was in 1968–69). (कर्नाटक — संतोष ट्रॉफी 2023)

• This was the first time that the knockout stage of the Santosh Trophy was hosted outside India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is India's premier national football championship for states and government institutions, started in 1941, and is organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• It is named after the late Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (present-day Bangladesh).

• West Bengal is the most successful team in the tournament's history.

NOTE

• Other important football trophies in India: Durand Cup (Asia's oldest football tournament, 1888), Rovers Cup, IFA Shield, Subroto Cup (school-level) and the Indian Super League (ISL) / I-League.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India?
option_1: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President.
option_2: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction
option_3: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
option_4: It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 129 of the Constitution declares that the Supreme Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court, including the power to punish for contempt of itself. (अनुच्छेद 129 — उच्चतम न्यायालय अभिलेख न्यायालय)

• A "court of record" means:

◦ Its judgments, proceedings and acts are recorded permanently and have evidentiary value — they cannot be questioned when produced before any court, and they are recognised as legal precedents.

◦ It has the power to punish for contempt of court (both civil and criminal contempt).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 143 — power of the President to consult the Supreme Court, i.e., its advisory jurisdiction. (Option 1)

• Article 131 — original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in disputes between the Centre and States or between States. (Option 2)

• Articles 132–134 — appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in constitutional, civil and criminal matters, making it the highest court of appeal. (Option 4)

• Article 215 gives the same "court of record" status to the High Courts.

NOTE

• Other key Supreme Court articles: Article 124 (establishment and constitution), Article 32 (writ jurisdiction — the "heart and soul" of the Constitution per Dr. B. R. Ambedkar), Article 137 (power of review), Article 141 (law declared by the SC is binding on all courts).

question: Indian classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj belonged to which of the following musical gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mewati Gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Hindustani classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj (1930–2020) belonged to the Mewati Gharana. (पंडित जसराज — मेवाती घराना)

• He is credited with popularising the Mewati Gharana worldwide and with creating the unique jugalbandi form "Jasrangi", in which a male and a female vocalist sing different ragas simultaneously.

• Honours: Padma Shri (1975), Padma Bhushan (1990) and Padma Vibhushan (2000). A minor planet (asteroid) 300128 Panditjasraj was named after him.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Patiala Gharana — associated with Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

• Dagar (Dagari) Gharana — associated with the Dhrupad style, e.g., the Dagar Brothers.

• Gwalior Gharana — the oldest gharana of Khayal singing, founded by Nathan Peer Bakhsh; associated with Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

NOTE

• Other major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Kirana Gharana (Abdul Karim Khan, Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal), Jaipur–Atrauli Gharana (Alladiya Khan, Kishori Amonkar), Agra Gharana and Rampur–Sahaswan Gharana.

question: Articles 29-30 of the Constitution of India deals with _______
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cultural and educational rights.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution of India together constitute the Cultural and Educational Rights, a part of the Fundamental Rights (Part III). (अनुच्छेद 29-30 — सांस्कृतिक और शैक्षिक अधिकार)

◦ Article 29 — Protection of the interests of minorities: any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it; and no citizen shall be denied admission to any State-maintained or State-aided educational institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.

◦ Article 30 — Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice; the State shall not discriminate against such institutions while granting aid.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights and their articles:

◦ Right to Equality — Articles 14–18

◦ Right to Freedom — Articles 19–22

◦ Right against Exploitation — Articles 23–24

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion — Articles 25–28

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights — Articles 29–30

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies — Article 32

NOTE

• The Right to Property (Article 31) was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300A.

• Article 21A (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002) makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years a Fundamental Right.

question: As per the 18th Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), the unemployment rate among females (aged 15 years and above) in urban areas declined to ________ in January-March 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9.2%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the 18th Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) quarterly bulletin, the unemployment rate among females aged 15 years and above in urban areas declined to 9.2% in the quarter January–March 2023 (from 10.1% in the same quarter a year earlier). (महिला बेरोज़गारी दर — 9.2%)

• The overall urban unemployment rate for persons aged 15+ fell to about 6.8% in that quarter.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was launched by the National Statistical Office (NSO) in April 2017 under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). It replaced the earlier quinquennial employment–unemployment surveys of the NSSO.

• Objectives of the PLFS:

◦ To estimate key employment indicators (WPR, LFPR, UR) in the short interval of three months for urban areas using the Current Weekly Status (CWS).

◦ To estimate the indicators annually for both rural and urban areas in usual status (ps+ss) and CWS.

NOTE

• Key terms: Unemployment Rate (UR) = percentage of unemployed persons among those in the labour force; Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) = percentage of persons in the labour force in the population; Worker Population Ratio (WPR) = percentage of employed persons in the population.

question: Which of the following is connected with daily atmospheric weather changes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Troposphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Troposphere" is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, and it is here that all weather phenomena — clouds, rain, fog, storms, thunder and lightning — occur. Hence it is connected with daily atmospheric weather changes. (क्षोभमंडल — मौसम की सभी घटनाएँ)

• Its average height is about 13 km — roughly 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator (greater at the equator due to strong convection currents).

• Temperature decreases with height in the troposphere at the normal lapse rate of about 6.5 °C per km.

• The upper boundary of the troposphere is called the "Tropopause".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Stratopause is the boundary between the stratosphere and the mesosphere; the stratosphere contains the ozone layer and is ideal for jet aircraft because it is free of turbulence.

• Lithosphere is the rigid outer shell of the Earth (crust + uppermost mantle), and the Asthenosphere is the semi-molten, plastic layer of the upper mantle below it — the source of magma. Neither is a part of the atmosphere.

NOTE

• Layers of the atmosphere from the surface upwards: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere (Ionosphere) → Exosphere.

• The Mesosphere is the coldest layer (about −100 °C at the mesopause) and is where meteors burn up; the Ionosphere reflects radio waves back to the Earth.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the lowest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the four given states, Tripura has the lowest literacy rate, at about 87.2%. (त्रिपुरा — सबसे कम साक्षरता दर, दिए गए विकल्पों में)

◦ Kerala — 94.0% (highest in India)

◦ Mizoram — 91.3% (second highest)

◦ Goa — 88.7%

◦ Tripura — 87.2%

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Overall literacy rate of India (2011) — 74.04%; male literacy — 82.14%, female literacy — 65.46%.

• Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate in India (61.8%), followed by Arunachal Pradesh and Rajasthan.

NOTE

• In the Census, a person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate.

• Other Census 2011 facts: most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest sex ratio — Haryana (879); highest density — Bihar (1106 persons/sq km).

question: In which state is the famous Brihadeshwar temple situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Brihadeshwar (Brihadisvara) Temple is situated at Thanjavur (Tanjore) in Tamil Nadu. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. (बृहदेश्वर मंदिर — तंजावुर, तमिलनाडु)

• It was built by the Chola emperor Rajaraja I in about 1010 CE, and is therefore also called the Rajarajeshvaram or the "Big Temple".

• It is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, with one of the tallest vimanas (about 66 m) in the world, topped by a massive monolithic capstone, and a huge Nandi carved out of a single rock.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The temple is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Great Living Chola Temples", which also includes the Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram (built by Rajendra I) and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram (built by Rajaraja II).

• Chola temple architecture is characterised by the vimana (tower over the sanctum), gopuram (gateway tower), mandapa (pillared hall) and prakara (enclosure).

NOTE

• Indian temple architecture styles: Nagara (North India — curvilinear shikhara), Dravida (South India — pyramidal vimana) and Vesara (Deccan — a hybrid of both, seen in Chalukya and Hoysala temples).

question: In which year did Robert Hooke introduce the term ‘cell’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1665.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English scientist Robert Hooke coined the term "cell" in 1665. (रॉबर्ट हुक — 1665 में 'कोशिका' शब्द)

• While examining a thin slice of cork under his self-designed compound microscope, he observed tiny box-like compartments that reminded him of the small rooms (cellulae) in a monastery — hence the name "cell".

• He published his observations in his famous book "Micrographia" (1665).

• What Hooke actually saw were only the dead cell walls of cork tissue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anton van Leeuwenhoek (1674) was the first to observe living cells (bacteria, protozoa, sperm) and is called the "Father of Microbiology".

• Robert Brown (1831) discovered the nucleus; Purkinje (1839) coined the term "protoplasm".

• The Cell Theory was proposed by M. J. Schleiden (1838) and Theodor Schwann (1839), and was completed by Rudolf Virchow (1855) with the statement "Omnis cellula-e cellula" — all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

NOTE

• The cell is the structural and functional unit of life. The largest cell is the ostrich egg; the longest cell in the human body is the nerve cell (neuron); the smallest cell is Mycoplasma (PPLO).

question: Which of the following is an example of capital receipt in the government budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sale of government bonds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Capital receipts" are those receipts of the government which either create a liability or reduce its assets. The sale of government bonds (market borrowing) creates a liability for the government (it must repay the principal with interest), and hence it is a capital receipt. (पूंजीगत प्राप्ति — सरकारी बॉण्ड की बिक्री)

• Two tests for a capital receipt:

◦ Does it create a liability? (borrowings, loans, small savings)

◦ Does it reduce an asset? (disinvestment, recovery of loans)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets. The other three options are revenue receipts:

◦ Tax revenue — income tax, GST, customs, corporation tax.

◦ Non-tax revenue — profits/dividends from government-owned enterprises (PSUs), interest receipts, fees and fines.

◦ Grants received from foreign countries — treated as non-tax revenue receipts because they need not be repaid.

• Main capital receipts: market borrowings, loans from the RBI and foreign governments, disinvestment proceeds, recovery of loans, small savings and provident funds.

NOTE

• Budget-related definitions: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings); Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts; Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement".

question: Which of the abhinayas deals with the use of costumes, jewellery, facial make-up etc?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aharya Abhinaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aharya Abhinaya" is the aspect of expression that deals with costumes, jewellery, ornaments, facial make-up, masks, stage properties and decoration. (आहार्य अभिनय — वेशभूषा एवं श्रृंगार)

• The Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni describes four types of Abhinaya (expression):

◦ Angika Abhinaya — expression through body movements, gestures (hastas/mudras), limbs and posture.

◦ Vachika Abhinaya — expression through speech, song, recitation and intonation.

◦ Aharya Abhinaya — expression through costume, make-up and ornamentation.

◦ Sattvika Abhinaya — expression of genuine inner emotion/psychological states (tears, trembling, change of colour, horripilation).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni, is the oldest and most authoritative treatise on Indian dramaturgy, dance and music, generally dated between the 2nd century BCE and the 2nd century CE. It is often called the "fifth Veda".

• It also expounds the Rasa theory — "Na bhavo rasa sambhavah" — the eight/nine Rasas (Shringara, Hasya, Karuna, Raudra, Veera, Bhayanaka, Bibhatsa, Adbhuta and Shanta).

NOTE

• Kathakali is the classical dance form best known for its elaborate Aharya Abhinaya — huge headgear, heavy costumes and colour-coded facial make-up (Pacha, Kathi, Thadi, Kari, Minukku).

question: Pandit Bhajan Sopori, who died in the year 2022, was a famous player of which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Bhajan Sopori (1948–2022) was a legendary Indian musician and a maestro of the "Santoor". (पंडित भजन सोपोरी — संतूर वादक)

• He belonged to the Sufiana Gharana of Kashmir and was often called the "Saint of the Santoor" and the "King of Strings".

• Honours: Padma Shri (2004) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. He composed music in several languages and worked as a composer with All India Radio.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer of Jammu and Kashmir, traditionally played with a pair of light wooden mallets (kalam). It has about 100 strings over bridges.

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is credited with bringing the Santoor from Kashmiri Sufiana music to the Hindustani classical concert stage.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian musical instruments (as per the Natya Shastra):

◦ Tata Vadya (stringed) — Sitar, Sarod, Veena, Santoor, Violin.

◦ Sushira Vadya (wind) — Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram.

◦ Avanaddha Vadya (percussion/membrane) — Tabla, Mridangam, Pakhawaj, Dholak.

◦ Ghana Vadya (solid/idiophones) — Manjira, Jaltarang, Ghatam.

• The Ravanahatha is an ancient bowed string instrument of Rajasthan.

question: Which of the following best defines transfer payments?
option_1: Payments made to individuals in exchange for their labour or services
option_2: Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services
option_3: Payments made by businesses to their shareholders as a share of profits
option_4: Payments made by individuals to the government in the form of taxes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Transfer payments" are unilateral (one-sided) payments made by the government to individuals for which no goods or services are received in return and no productive activity takes place. (हस्तांतरण भुगतान)

◦ Examples: old-age pensions, unemployment allowances, scholarships, subsidies, disaster relief, widow pensions.

• Because nothing is produced in exchange, transfer payments are NOT included in the calculation of National Income (GDP/GNP) — including them would amount to double counting.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes factor payments — wages/salaries paid in exchange for labour, which are included in national income.

• Option 3 describes dividends, which are a distribution of company profits to shareholders (a factor income to owners of capital).

• Option 4 describes taxes, which are compulsory payments from citizens to the government.

NOTE

• Factor income vs Transfer income: factor income (rent, wages, interest, profit) is earned by contributing to production; transfer income is received without any contribution to production.

• National income is measured by three methods: the Value Added (Product) Method, the Income Method and the Expenditure Method. In India, national income is estimated by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Red Earth and Pouring Rain: A Novel’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Chandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Red Earth and Pouring Rain: A Novel" (1995) was written by the Indian-American author Vikram Chandra. (विक्रम चंद्रा)

• The novel won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize for Best First Book and the David Higham Prize for Fiction. Its title is drawn from a classical Tamil Sangam poem (Kuruntokai).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other works of Vikram Chandra: "Love and Longing in Bombay", "Sacred Games" (adapted into a popular web series) and "Geek Sublime".

• Shashi Tharoor — "The Great Indian Novel", "An Era of Darkness", "Why I Am a Hindu", "India: From Midnight to the Millennium".

• Ashwin Sanghi — "The Rozabal Line", "Chanakya's Chant", "The Krishna Key" (writer of mytho-historical thrillers).

• Ruskin Bond — "The Room on the Roof", "The Blue Umbrella", "A Flight of Pigeons", "Rusty" series.

NOTE

• Frequently asked Indian authors and books: Arundhati Roy — "The God of Small Things" (Booker Prize 1997); Aravind Adiga — "The White Tiger" (Booker Prize 2008); Salman Rushdie — "Midnight's Children"; Amitav Ghosh — "The Shadow Lines", "The Hungry Tide"; Kiran Desai — "The Inheritance of Loss".

question: The Nuakhai festival of ______________ is observed on Panchami Tithi (fifth day) of the lunar fortnight of Bhadrava (August-September), the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nuakhai" is an agricultural/harvest festival of Odisha, celebrated mainly in Western Odisha (the Sambalpur–Kalahandi–Bolangir region) and in adjoining areas of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. (नुआखाई — ओडिशा)

• It is observed on the Panchami Tithi (fifth day) of the bright fortnight of the month of Bhadrava (Bhadrab, August–September), i.e., the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.

• The word "Nua" means new and "Khai" means food/eating — so the festival marks the ceremonial eating of the newly harvested rice, first offered to the presiding deity (e.g., Goddess Samaleswari of Sambalpur).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Odisha: Rath Yatra (Puri), Raja Parba, Durga Puja, Konark Dance Festival, Bali Jatra, Dhanu Jatra.

• Harvest festivals of India: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Makar Sankranti (many states), Lohri (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), Baisakhi (Punjab), Onam (Kerala), Wangala (Meghalaya — the Garo harvest festival), Nabanna (West Bengal).

NOTE

• Nuakhai is preceded by nine ritual steps (Behrana, Lagna dekha, Daka haka, Sapha sutura, Ghina bika, Nua dhana, Bali paka, Nuakhai and Juhar bhet), ending with "Nuakhai Juhar" — the exchange of greetings and respect among family members.

question: Which country is hosting the ICC 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (ODI World Cup) was hosted by India from 5 October to 19 November 2023. (आईसीसी विश्व कप 2023 — भारत)

• It was the 13th edition of the tournament and the first time India hosted the ODI World Cup solely (earlier editions in 1987, 1996 and 2011 were co-hosted).

• The final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad — the world's largest cricket stadium (capacity about 1,32,000) — where Australia defeated India to win their sixth title.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Player of the Tournament 2023 — Virat Kohli (765 runs, a record in a single World Cup); Mohammed Shami was the leading wicket-taker (24 wickets).

• Past ODI World Cup winners: 1975 & 1979 — West Indies; 1983 & 2011 — India; 1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015, 2023 — Australia; 1992 — Pakistan; 1996 — Sri Lanka; 2019 — England.

NOTE

• The International Cricket Council (ICC) was founded in 1909 (as the Imperial Cricket Conference) and has its headquarters at Dubai, UAE.

• India won the 1983 World Cup under Kapil Dev at Lord's and the 2011 World Cup under MS Dhoni at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Playing It My Way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Playing It My Way" (published in 2014) is the autobiography of the legendary Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, co-written with Boria Majumdar. (सचिन तेंदुलकर की आत्मकथा)

• It was released shortly after his retirement from international cricket in November 2013 and set a record for pre-publication bookings for an adult hardback in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sachin Tendulkar — the "Master Blaster" / "God of Cricket":

◦ The only player with 100 international centuries and the first to score a double century in ODIs (2010, vs South Africa).

◦ He is the highest run-scorer in both Tests (15,921) and ODIs (18,426).

◦ Awards: Arjuna Award (1994), Khel Ratna (1997-98), Padma Shri (1999), Padma Vibhushan (2008) and the Bharat Ratna (2014) — the first sportsperson to receive it.

• Option 1 "Unbreakable" is the autobiography of the boxer Mary Kom.

• Option 4 "I Am No Messiah" is the autobiography of the actor Sonu Sood.

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies: "Ace Against Odds" (Sania Mirza), "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "A Century Is Not Enough" (Sourav Ganguly), "Sunny Days" (Sunil Gavaskar), "Courage and Conviction" (Gen. V. K. Singh).

question: In April 2023, Tamil Nadu passed a bill banning which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Online Gambling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2023, the Tamil Nadu Assembly re-passed the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Online Gambling and Regulation of Online Games Bill, which bans online gambling and games of chance played for money, such as online rummy and online poker. (तमिलनाडु — ऑनलाइन जुए पर प्रतिबंध)

• The Bill was first passed in October 2022, returned by the Governor, and then re-adopted by the Assembly in April 2023 before receiving assent, becoming an Act in 2023.

• The law prescribes imprisonment and fines for those who run or advertise such online gambling platforms and provides for the constitution of an Online Gaming Authority to regulate online games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The move followed a series of suicides linked to losses in online rummy in Tamil Nadu.

• Betting and gambling fall under Entry 34 of the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, so States are competent to legislate on the subject.

• Under Article 200, a Governor may withhold assent or return a Bill for reconsideration; if the House passes it again, the Governor "shall not withhold assent".

NOTE

• Other states that have banned online gambling/real-money games at various times: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Assam, Nagaland and Karnataka (Karnataka's law was struck down by the High Court).

question: In which stadium was the final match of ODI Cricket World Cup 2011 played?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wankhede Stadium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final of the ICC Cricket World Cup 2011 was played at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011. (वानखेड़े स्टेडियम, मुंबई)

• India defeated Sri Lanka by 6 wickets to lift the trophy for the second time (after 1983). Captain MS Dhoni finished the match with a famous six and scored an unbeaten 91, winning the Player of the Match award.

• Yuvraj Singh was adjudged the Player of the Tournament (362 runs and 15 wickets).

• The 2011 World Cup was co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Wankhede Stadium is the home ground of the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) and was built in 1974; it is named after Sheshrao Wankhede.

• Eden Gardens (Kolkata) is India's oldest and largest cricket stadium (established 1864), managed by the Cricket Association of Bengal.

• Feroz Shah Kotla (now Arun Jaitley Stadium), Delhi is the venue where Anil Kumble took all 10 wickets in an innings against Pakistan in 1999.

NOTE

• India's World Cup wins: 1983 (ODI, at Lord's, under Kapil Dev), 2007 (T20 World Cup, at Johannesburg, under MS Dhoni), 2011 (ODI, at Wankhede, under MS Dhoni) and 2024 (T20 World Cup, at Barbados, under Rohit Sharma).

question: ‘Mitra Mela’ was a revolutionary organisation founded by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinayak Savarkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mitra Mela" was a secret revolutionary society founded in 1899 at Nasik by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (along with his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar). (मित्र मेला — विनायक दामोदर सावरकर)

• In 1904, the Mitra Mela was reorganised and renamed "Abhinav Bharat Society" (Young India Society), inspired by Mazzini's "Young Italy".

• Its aim was to achieve complete independence through armed revolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• V. D. Savarkar (1883–1966) wrote "The Indian War of Independence, 1857", in which he described the Revolt of 1857 as the first war of Indian independence. He was sentenced to two life terms (50 years) and imprisoned in the Cellular Jail, Port Blair (Kala Pani).

• Khudiram Bose, along with Prafulla Chaki, carried out the Muzaffarpur bomb attack (1908) aimed at Magistrate Kingsford, and was hanged in 1908 at the age of 18.

NOTE

• Important revolutionary organisations: Anushilan Samiti (1902, Kolkata — Barindra Ghosh, Pramathanath Mitra), Yugantar (1906), Abhinav Bharat (1904, Nasik), India House (London, 1905 — Shyamji Krishna Varma), Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco — Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna), HRA (1924, Kanpur) and HSRA (1928, Delhi).

question: Which is the Gaussian unit of kinematic viscosity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stokes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stokes (St)" is the CGS/Gaussian unit of kinematic viscosity. (स्टोक्स — गतिज श्यानता का मात्रक)

◦ 1 stokes = 1 cm²/s = 10⁻⁴ m²/s.

• Kinematic viscosity (ν) = dynamic viscosity (η) / density (ρ). Its SI unit is m²/s.

• The unit is named after the Irish physicist Sir George Gabriel Stokes, who also gave Stokes' law for the drag force on a small sphere moving through a viscous fluid: F = 6πηrv.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CGS unit of dynamic (absolute) viscosity is the poise (P); 1 poise = 0.1 Pa·s. Its SI unit is the pascal-second (Pa·s) or N·s/m².

• Ampere is the SI unit of electric current; Joule is the SI unit of work/energy/heat; Darcy is a unit of permeability of a porous medium used in geology and petroleum engineering.

NOTE

• Viscosity is the internal friction/resistance of a fluid to flow. Viscosity of liquids decreases with a rise in temperature, whereas the viscosity of gases increases with a rise in temperature.

• The terminal velocity of a body falling through a viscous fluid is derived from Stokes' law; it is directly proportional to the square of the radius of the body.

question: Who among the following freedom fighter lawyers from Bengal is known as Deshbandhu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chittaranjan Das (1870–1925), the eminent lawyer and freedom fighter from Bengal, is popularly known as "Deshbandhu" ("Friend of the Nation"). (देशबंधु — चित्तरंजन दास)

• As a lawyer he shot to fame by successfully defending Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908).

• He gave up his lucrative legal practice to join the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) and presided over the Gaya session of the Indian National Congress (1922).

• Along with Motilal Nehru, he founded the Swaraj Party in 1923, which sought to enter the legislative councils and obstruct the government from within.

• He was the first Mayor of the Calcutta Corporation (1924), with Subhas Chandra Bose as the Chief Executive Officer. Subhas Chandra Bose regarded him as his political guru.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bipin Chandra Pal was one of the trio "Lal-Bal-Pal" (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal) of the Extremist/Assertive phase; he is called the "Father of Revolutionary Thoughts in India".

• Durga Mohan Das was a Brahmo social reformer known for his work on women's education and widow remarriage; Satish Ranjan Das was a noted lawyer and the founder of the Doon School.

NOTE

• Popular titles of freedom fighters: Mahatma/Bapu — M. K. Gandhi; Lokmanya — B. G. Tilak; Netaji — Subhas Chandra Bose; Punjab Kesari — Lala Lajpat Rai; Sardar/Iron Man — Vallabhbhai Patel; Frontier Gandhi — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan; Gurudev — Rabindranath Tagore; Rajaji — C. Rajagopalachari.
